findings.summary: xAI awarded $200M Pentagon contract for Grok AI in military systems, including classified access
findings.detail: In July 2025, Pentagon awarded xAI $200M contract to provide Grok AI to 3 million military personnel. In February 2026, xAI signed agreement for Grok access to classified Pentagon systems — previously only Anthropic Claude had classified access. xAI agreed to 'all lawful purposes' standard that Anthropic refused (Anthropic blocked mass surveillance and autonomous weapons use). DOGE staff reportedly spent months pushing agencies to adopt Grok before contract. Sen. Warren demanded investigation in September 2025.

findings.summary: xAI replaced Anthropic for classified Pentagon AI access; Anthropic refused 'all lawful purposes' standard blocking mass surveillance and autonomous weapons
findings.detail: Prior to xAI's classified access deal, Anthropic's Claude was the only AI model available in classified Pentagon systems used for sensitive intelligence work, weapons development, and battlefield operations. Anthropic lost this position because it refused the Pentagon's demand to make Claude available for 'all lawful purposes,' specifically blocking mass surveillance of Americans and development of fully autonomous weapons. xAI's Grok agreed to the 'all lawful purposes' standard. This represents a significant policy choice: the Pentagon chose an AI company willing to remove ethical guardrails over one that maintained them. OpenAI and Google also in talks for classified access.

findings.summary: xAI has multiple SEC Form D filings through fund vehicles managed by Sydecar LLC (a fund administration platform). Identified entities: xAI 2 May 2024 (CIK 2026824, filed Jun 2024), xAi a Series of OORI LLC (CIK 2054050, filed Jan 2025), xAI 2025(1) (CIK 2080444, filed Aug 2025), xAI 2025(2) (CIK 2102114, filed Dec 2025, .5K offering, 3 investors), xAI Grain Ventures Jan 2026 (CIK 2109943, filed Feb 2026, .5K offering, 11 investors). All registered at 2093 Philadelphia Pike, Claymont DE 19703 (registered agent address). These are small SPV fund vehicles, not xAI's primary fundraising. xAI Corp itself is not a registered SEC entity.

Notable FEC finding: Marc Tessier-Lavigne, listed as CEO at xAI, made a ,300 contribution to Liccardo for Congress. Tessier-Lavigne is the former Stanford president who resigned in 2023 amid research misconduct allegations. His appearance as xAI CEO in FEC records (employer field) is a significant personnel connection. Also: xAI employees show predominantly small Democratic donations (ActBlue), with AI tutors making up a large portion of identifiable xAI donor-employees.
